questions.title: Minimum Window Substring
questions.description:
You are given two lines of input, each containing only lowercase letters and no spaces:

- **Line 1** — the `haystack` string.
- **Line 2** — the `needle` string.

Print the **shortest contiguous substring** of `haystack` that contains every character of `needle`, **including duplicates**. If `needle` contains a character `k` times, the window you print must contain that character **at least `k` times** — not merely at least once. Characters of `needle` do **not** need to appear in the same order inside the window, and they do **not** need to be contiguous with each other inside the window — they just need to each occur enough times somewhere within it (the window itself is always a single contiguous slice of `haystack`).

If several windows of the shortest length all qualify, print the one that **starts earliest** in `haystack`.

If no window of `haystack` contains `needle` (with full multiplicity), print exactly:

```
NONE
```

### Worked example

Input:
```
adobecodebanc
abc
```

Output:
```
banc
```

`"banc"` is the shortest window of `haystack` containing at least one `a`, one `b` and one `c`.

### Multiplicity matters

If `needle` is `"aa"`, a window containing only a single `a` does **not** qualify — it must contain at least two `a`s. Don't just check which distinct characters are present; count how many of each the needle requires and make sure the window has at least that many of each.

testCases.description: repeated needle char: window must contain 2 a's, not just 1 (set-based solutions return "a")
repeated needle char forces a much longer window than a set-based solution would find
tie between two equally short windows; earliest start must win, and window order need not match needle order
NONE: a needle character never appears in haystack at all
NONE: needle character is present but not enough times
needle equal to the entire haystack
